disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Combined Presentation, is characterized by a persistent pattern of both inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development across multiple settings (e.g., home, school, work). Symptoms begin in childhood, though many individuals are not diagnosed until adolescence or adulthood, especially if they have developed compensatory strategies or chosen environments that partly mask their difficulties. The course tends to be chronic, with hyperactive behaviors often becoming more internalized (e.g., restlessness) over time, while inattention and disorganization frequently remain prominent and impairing. ADHD is distinguished from anxiety, mood, and personality disorders by its early onset, cross-situational pattern, and core deficits in sustained attention, executive functioning, and impulse control rather than primarily affective or situational triggers.

narrative.stressor: Over the past several years of retirement, Antonio’s loosely structured days had suited his lifelong tendency to jump between gardening, painting, cooking experiments, and community storytelling without much formal planning. About 14 months ago, his wife developed mobility issues after a minor stroke, and Antonio took on managing her appointments, medications, and insurance paperwork in addition to coordinating the neighborhood garden and youth storytelling projects. The increased load of schedules, forms, and follow-through exposed longstanding but previously manageable organizational difficulties, leading to repeated missed appointments, double-booked commitments, and mounting tension at home when his wife felt she could not rely on him for practical tasks despite his obvious devotion. After a frustrated primary care visit where Antonio admitted he felt "scattered" and overwhelmed by basic daily responsibilities despite being otherwise physically well, his doctor referred him for a psychiatric evaluation to explore attention and planning problems that had become clearly impairing in his caregiving and community roles.
narrative.chief_complaint: I keep forgetting everyday things like appointments and errands, and it’s starting to really mess up taking care of my wife and my commitments in the garden project.

narrative.stressor: In her final year of college and into her budding role at the biotech startup, Sherryann had managed to push through by relying on last-minute surges of energy, all-night coding sessions, and teammates who helped her clean up disorganized work. About a year and a bit ago, as project expectations increased and she was given more independent responsibility for data pipelines and deliverables, her relaxed approach to time management stopped working; missed deadlines and half-finished analyses led to formal performance warnings and ultimately a "mutual" decision for her to step away from the role. Losing the job shook her confidence and made her notice how often she was derailed when trying to focus, even on projects she cared about, which also contributed to her delaying applications for new positions and dropping the ball on volunteer commitments and social plans. After a mentor from a STEM outreach event gently suggested that her long-standing struggles with organization and follow-through might be more than "just being scattered," she agreed to seek a psychiatric assessment to understand why she could not seem to complete tasks reliably despite motivation and ability.
narrative.chief_complaint: I start projects and assignments full of ideas, but I just can’t seem to follow through and finish things, and it’s already cost me my first job.

narrative.stressor: Daniel was promoted to supervise a larger sales territory about 14 months ago, a move that aligned with his ambitions toward regional management and consulting but also dramatically increased the volume of meetings, reports, and travel logistics he had to juggle. The new role demanded sustained attention to detailed performance metrics, careful sequencing of follow-ups, and long strategy sessions—environments where his tendency to mentally drift into creative ideas or guitar riffs in his head began to clash with expectations for focus and consistency. Over the following year, he found that despite his strong interpersonal skills and innovative training concepts, he was repeatedly missing key details in contracts, overlooking action items from meetings, and struggling to keep his mind from wandering during crucial calls, which contributed to friction with upper management and added strain during an already difficult marital separation. After his supervisor commented that his "head seems somewhere else half the time" and suggested coaching, Daniel, recognizing a lifelong pattern that was now clearly jeopardizing his career plans, requested a referral to a psychiatrist to find out why he was having so much trouble staying mentally present when it mattered most.
narrative.chief_complaint: My mind keeps drifting off in meetings and calls, and I get distracted so easily that it’s starting to hurt my performance as a supervisor.
